Author: K.Suresh Reddy
Bench: K.Suresh Reddy
 The Hon'Ble Sri Justice K.Suresh Reddy
 Writ Petition No. 3545 Of 2021
Order:

Heard Sri S.Ravi, learned senior counsel, appearing on behalf of Sri Pavan Kumar Annabathuni,
learned counsel appearing for the petitioners, learned Government Pleader for Agriculture appearing for respondent Nos. 1 and 2 and Sri Sai Sanjay Suraneni, learned counsel appearing for respondent No. 3.

2. The grievance of the petitioners in the present writ petition is that in spite of there being material that use of Ethephon (Ethylene ripener sachets) is not objectionable for ripening fruits, respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are either interfering with or discouraging the said use.

3. Learned senior counsel submits that use of Ethephon in powder form was approved by Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (hereinafter referred to as 'FSSAI') by Guidance Note No.
04/2018.

entities.text: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: The said Ethephon chemical produces Ethylene gas which is not a banned substance.
Earlier, the farmer communities use Calcium Carbide gas also known as Acetylene gas for ripening fruits.
The said Calcium Carbide gas was banned by Government in 1970's.
In spite of the same, all the traders are using the said Calcium Carbide.
It is only after various pronouncements by different High Courts, Government has taken steps to implement the ban on using Calcium Carbide.
It is only thereafter, farmer communities started using Ethylene gas chambers for ripening fruits.
As it costs lot of expenditure, products like En-ripe and Ethephon, i.e. products of respondent No. 3 and the petitioners respectively, came into existence for ripening fruits.
Of course, both of them are not banned by Government and both the products are approved by FSSAI.

In spite of the same,
respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are either encouraging the product of respondent No. 3 i.e. En-ripe or interfering with the business activities of the petitioners.

4. In support of his contentions, learned senior counsel places reliance on Nalin Venkat Kishore Kumar and another Vs. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and others1, wherein a Division Bench of the High Court for the State of Telangana, after considering all the aspects,
permitted to use both En-ripe and Ethephon as both of them are approved by FSSAI and also places reliance on a judgment of the High Court of Delhi in Shivashish Dwivedi and another Vs. Food Safety and Standards Authority of India and others2.

sentences.text: 1 5. On the other hand, learned Government Pleader for Agriculture filed counter affidavit on behalf of respondent No. 2.

Paragraph Nos. 6 to 12 of the said counter affidavit read thus:
"6. Further, it is respectfully submitted that, the Indian Institute of Horticulture Research (IIHR), the premier Institute under ICAR has conducted trails and recommended En-ripe for safe Ripening of fruits.

Hence, the Department of Horticulture encouraged Ethylene gas WP (PIL) No. 176 OF 2020 & BATCH DATED 19-01-2022 WP (C) No. 13025 OF 2018 DATED 30-01-2020 and En-ripe as an alternative to the Calcium Carbide in ripening of the fruits as a part of technology dissemination, and there is no intension of prejudice/discrimination.

entities.text: Department of Horticulture encouraged Ethylene gas
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text: 7. Further, it is respectfully submitted that, with regard to organizing Demos, the Department has not given any instructions to the field staff to organize any demos with En-ripe product.
It is also to submit that, the Department has not entered into any kind of procurement of En-ripe from the company/supplier and also not promoting En- ripe as it is only alternative.
The Department intension is very clear and En-ripe is one of the safe alternatives together with other recommended products for ripening as recommended by IIHR-ICAR, Bangalore.
8. Further, it is to submit that, FSSAI made it clear that only permitted forms of Ethephon be used and great care needs to be taken to prevent it for coming into direct contact with the fruit.
Ethephon is highly toxic organo phosphorous chemical and also considered to be posing grave health threat.
It is registered as an insecticide/pesticide under Insecticide Act and Rules and given its serious potential threat to human health and environment.

Insecticide Rules, 1971, have extensive restrictions on its mode of use, protective clothing to be worm by workers and its transport and use, but these are frequently floated, due to various factors in the field.
9. In this regard, though Ethephon is permitted, there are restrictions in its use provided that the powder packed in the sachets should not come into contact with fruits.

There are many chances during handling, packaging of fruits, transport etc,
that the sachets may get open/break and it may come into contact of fruits which is not advisable.

10. Further, Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, New Delhi, India, has mentioned in its conclusions on the study on Ethephon that the observations in the Liver are probably indicative of degenerative changes associated with Ethephon and it has hepatotaxic potential.

entities.text: Institute of Liver and Biliary Sciences, New Delhi
entities.label: ORG

sentences.text:
11. In this regard, it is respectfully submitted that, based on the above reports and also as Food Safety and Health Security should be the top concern of any Government for its citizens, and also present safe alternatives of Calcium Carbide, the use of Ethylene gas based ripening chambers and En-ripe (as recommended by IIHR)
the Department of Horticulture issued instructions to disseminate the information Goldripe International Pvt. Ltd., vs The State Of Andhra Pradesh on 11 August, 2022 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/116882352/
2 among the farming community and traders involved in the process.

sentences.text: 12. Further, it is respectfully submitted that, the Department has neither given permission for marketing any products nor imposed any restrictions on sale and use of any chemicals used for ripening of fruits.
And the matter is not in the purview of this Department."
Learned Government Pleader, on instructions, submits that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 will not interfere with the business activities of the petitioners so long as the said product is not banned.
Learned Government Pleader further submits that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are also not encouraging farmer communities to use any particular product.
6. This Court perused the entire material on record.
In the letter addressed by respondent No. 2 to Government, he did not encourage or recommend any particular product.

But in the last paragraph of the impugned memo dated 20-03-2020, respondent No. 2 requested all the DDHs/ADHs/HOs to appraise the farmers about the benefits of En-ripe together with the importance of using ripening chambers to avoid using Calcium Carbide and Ethephon for ripening of fruits.

So far as the use of Ethephon sachets is concerned, FSSAI already issued certain guidelines permitting maximum concentration of Ethylene gas to 100 ppm for artificial ripening of fruits and every sachet must be packed in a 40-60 micron cellulose membrane paper or its equivalent and every precaution has to be taken to prevent leakage.

However, it is averred in the counter affidavit that respondent Nos. 1 and 2 are not encouraging any particular product either to use Ethephon or En-ripe and that they are not interfering with the petitioners in selling Ethephon in sachets as well as per the guidelines prescribed by FSSAI.
7.
In the light of the above and in view of the averments made in the counter affidavit, the writ petition is allowed setting aside the impugned memo dated 20-03-2020 issued by respondent No. 2.
Pending miscellaneous applications, if any, shall stand closed in consequence.
No costs.
